chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'A'ala, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about cupping for the fasting person. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he does not fear weakness.'

key_terms.حِجَامَة: Cupping (a therapeutic procedure involving suction cups)

ai.seo_question: Is cupping permissible for a fasting person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that cupping (*hijamah*) does not inherently break the fast, establishing the principle of *al-asl al-suhhah* (presumption of validity) unless specific harm is anticipated. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the fast remains valid as long as the procedure does not lead to significant weakness (*da'f*) that would necessitate breaking the fast for health reasons, distinguishing it from practices that cause immediate nullification.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the cupping for the Fasting one. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when he does not fear weakness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
Can a man apply cupping when he is fasting?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, if he is not afraid of weakness.’”
